The launch surface should commit its own bootstrap output on the run branch (or validate should ignore the spec folder).

Story 20-1 dev session (all legs Opus 5.5): 5.92M tokens (788k weighted), ~7 min wall-clock, landed attempt 1 with deviation score 1, and caught a real Linux-only test defect (DW-4).

payload.description: Loop deficiency: a dev session named its story spec <id>.md instead of <id>-<slug>.md (story 21-6). bmad-loop v0.9.1 resolves a spec by the glob <id>-*.md, so it read the finished, committed story as pending, logged a result-less Stop (verdict pending) and armed the stall grace. Closed by hand: git mv to <id>-<slug>.md and a commit. Hole to plug: the studio customization (bmad-build-auto.toml) or the manifest's invoke_dev_with should pin the spec file name, and the pre_commit gate should refuse a stories/ file that does not match <id>-*.md.

Loop deficiency: Claude Code 2.1.283 showed the dialog 'Make auto mode your default permission mode?' inside a bmad-loop dev session started with --permission-mode bypassPermissions. The engine's stall nudge was typed into that dialog, which answered it: the sandbox's ~/.claude/settings.json gained permissions.defaultMode=auto at 21:11:02Z and the live session switched to auto mode. The nudge text never reached the agent. Hole to plug: provision-engine.sh should pre-answer the dialog in the sandbox's user settings, and the runbook should name the setting.

Loop deficiency (bmad-loop v0.9.1, upstream candidate): the dev-stall grace re-arms on any growth of the tee'd pane log, and Claude Code's rotating footer tips grow that log while the session is idle. After the first stall nudge the second one never fired (stall_nudges_sent stayed 1 for 14+ minutes), so session_timeout_min was the only bound on an idle finished session.

Loop deficiency: the supervisor's machine-local policy.toml keeps the engine template's max_tokens_per_story=2000000, while every Opus 5.5 story measured 3.9M to 4.4M weighted tokens (21-4: 3.86M, 21-5: 4.40M). Each story journals token-budget-exceeded. kb/execution-pipeline-model-routing.md records 5000000 as the value that held. Hole to plug: tk-studio-launch or pipeline.py apply should check the policy limits against the budget bands and report a mismatch.

Loop deficiency: an sbx engine reads the Windows host checkout, where files under '* text=auto' are CRLF. TUA's verify gate was red on 2 of 1030 tests (golden .tss compared on LF) in the sandbox and would be on the host; the main PC's WSL clone is LF and hid it. Fixed per project by pinning the format to LF (the-universe-awaits PR #2). Hole to plug: tk-studio onboarding or activate should report text formats a project's tests read byte-exact that are not pinned to LF when the project has an sbx engine.

Loop deficiency: story spec files are named <id>-<slug>.md where the id already carries the title slug, so names reach about 150 characters. A clone of the supervisor under a deep folder fails on Windows with 'Filename too long' (MAX_PATH); host verification needs a short-path clone such as «path»<name>. Hole to plug: the task-planning instructions could use short ids (21-6) for file names, or the runbook could set core.longpaths.
payload.evidence: host clone for the 21-5 Windows check, 2026-09-28

payload.description: Loop deficiency: the engine lives only as long as one host-side 'sbx exec' started from a Claude desktop-app session on the agent PC. If that app restarts, the sandbox stops and the engine dies mid-story. Story 22.3 (start.ps1 holds the engine) owns the fix; until then, check the holder process after any app restart on Tim-PC-2.
payload.evidence: tk-studio-supervisor Epic 21 launch5, host pid of sbx exec, 2026-09-28

payload.description: Loop deficiency: story 21-5 landed with a race in its signal path (handlers installed after spawn() returned), and its own signal tests passed at its gate by timing. One story later the same tests were red in the engine on every run, the 21-6 review session could not find the cause, consult ruled escalate, and the run paused. Closed by hand: root cause found with timing marks in a scratch copy, fixed in 76ded1b with a test that fails 15 of 15 on the old code. Hole to plug: the verify gate should run process and signal tests more than once (or under a repeat flag) before a story lands, and the consult instructions should name 'run the failing test N times on the baseline and record the failure rate' as the first step on verify-red.

Loop deficiency: when a run pauses on an escalation after the story's work is committed, the engine's close-out never runs: no studio gate (reconcile), no post_commit meter, no follow-up-review deferral, no squash. Closing story 21-6 by hand took seven steps (commit the pending pass, fix, verify on both hosts, spec status and resolution, reconcile and replan notes, meter from the run dir, trial data and archive). Hole to plug: a studio script or tk-studio-launch verb that closes a landed story by hand in one step, from the runbook's 'when a run pauses' list.

Loop deficiency: a headless tk-studio-launch session (epic-22-launch1, Opus 5.5) wrote SPEC.md, met the dirty tree at its second readiness check, and ended by asking the operator for permission to commit. It printed no status block (AD-11: never a question, always the block). The Epic 24 launch committed its own bootstrap; the Epic 20 launch ended blocked. Three launches, three behaviours. Hole to plug: tk-studio-launch should state one rule for its own bootstrap output (commit it on the run branch, then re-check), and conformance should drive the dirty-tree case.

Loop deficiency: story 22-2 landed with a test that fails only on Windows (test/page.test.ts expects '~/planted-home-file'; on win32 the page shows '~\planted-home-file'). The engine's gate runs on Linux only, so it was green. The Windows host run after the story caught it; the product behaviour is right and the fix is one line in the test. Third Windows-only finding after the canonicalPath case fold (21-4) and DW-5. Hole to plug: a Windows leg in the verify gate, for example the supervisor's host tier running 'bun test' in a clone of the story commit before the story is accepted.

Loop deficiency: story 22-3 enabled the end-to-end suites on win32 and wrote their win32 paths from Linux, where they cannot run. The first Windows host run failed 29 of 548 tests. Every cause was test-side: .cmd fakes cannot be spawned without a shell (EINVAL), a killed process reports exit code 1 not SIGKILL, bun's folder also holds uv under WinGet, symlinks need a privilege, and the fake sbx used the VM folder as a host folder. Closed by hand in 39596da (no production change); the host is 545 pass, 16 skip, 0 fail. Hole to plug: the same Windows leg as the verify gate needs; a story that touches win32 paths cannot be accepted on a Linux run alone.

payload.description: Loop deficiency: after 'winget upgrade Docker.sbx' (v0.45.1 to v0.47.0) the daemon was stopped on purpose, and a plain 'sbx ls' issued from a Claude desktop-app session auto-started a new daemon inside the app's container context. That daemon read the sandbox records but could not reach the inner docker engine ('docker daemon is not reachable at «path»'), listed no sandboxes, and every 'sbx exec' failed with 'backend unavailable'. Closed by hand: 'sbx daemon stop', then the 'Docker Sandboxes daemon' logon task (Start-ScheduledTask), which starts it outside the app context. Hole to plug: from a Claude session, run no sbx command but 'sbx daemon status' while the daemon may be down ('sbx ls', 'exec', 'rm' and 'diagnose' all auto-start one); runbook section 3.5 and the sbx-engine scripts should probe 'sbx daemon status' first and refuse to continue when it is not running; also 'schtasks /Run /TN' from Git Bash is rewritten as paths (MSYS), use PowerShell Start-ScheduledTask.

Claude Code 2.1.292 added an `effort` parameter to the Agent tool and workflow agents to the agent.spawn mod hook — Evaluate passing an explicit effort level from tk-studio-job dispatch notes when invoking review/research agents, to trade cost against depth per job type.

Claude Code Mods system launched — plugins can now rewrite deeper agent behavior — No studio dependency change — Mods are a host-level customization surface, not a plugin-authoring primitive the studio's skills currently need; revisit if a future studio surface wants a persistent side-watcher instead of a job-triggered review skill.

payload.description: Loop deficiency: host-tier skill jobs (supervisor, claude -p --permission-mode auto) ended blocked three times with 'This command requires approval' on the studio's own uv run script, even after permissions.allow [Bash(uv run:*)] was added to the project's tracked .claude/settings.json. Root cause: Claude Code applies a project's permission rules only in a folder whose trust dialog was accepted on the box (exact repo root, no parent inheritance), and the supervisor and TUA folders had never been trusted on the agent PC; a headless run cannot answer the dialog. Closed by hand: the operator opened claude once in each repo and accepted; the next studio-health run ended complete with no denial. Hole to plug: onboarding and provisioning should check projects[root].hasTrustDialogAccepted in ~/.claude.json for every registered project and report an untrusted one as a drift (the drift check can read it without writing); the runbook now says to trust every repo once (sections 4.1, 4.6, 8).
payload.evidence: runs q-studio-health-20261009T045710Z-29ca5b, -050354Z-ea37da, -050812Z-f1f81c blocked (denied); -051830Z-bae5d4 complete after trust; probes: the same rule allowed in trusted «path» ignored in untrusted «path» CLI 2.1.284 function Uge(e) = projects[e].hasTrustDialogAccepted exact lookup

payload.description: Proposal: adopt Claude Code's advisor tool as a routing leg. The advisor (experimental server tool, Anthropic API, Claude Code 2.1.260+ in -p) is the harness-native form of the loop's consult leg: a stronger model consulted at decision points with the full conversation. Proposal: an advisor field per pipeline leg (off by default) applied as --advisor on the session and forwarded to implementer and reviewer launches; consult triggers restated as advisor instructions with a Consult Log entry per call; the meter extended to price advisor tokens; a third arm in Epic 24.3 (Sonnet 5.5 main + Opus 5.5 advisor). Human escalation and the gate unchanged. Risks: uncapped uncached full-transcript reads, subagent inheritance, feature-flag fetching, Fable consent.

payload.description: Loop deficiency candidate 16 (found while planning the one-repository migration, ADR proposed AD-21): the supervisor holds one lock per checkout and the loop commits on a run branch in the mounted checkout, so once the plugin and the supervisor share «path» their two loops cannot run concurrently; one blocks on the other's lock for hours, and a run that switches branches under the other's working tree would corrupt it. The studio's project model also assumes a project root equals a checkout root (registry root, launch-epic ROOT, folder trust, hooks under CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR), which a nested root at apps/supervisor must be proven to satisfy. Fix to make: the supervisor launches each sandboxed run in its own git worktree of the checkout (worktree per run branch, removed at close-out, never following junctions), the lock becomes per worktree, and onboarding plus the drift check accept and verify nested project roots inside one repository; rehearse before the migration cut-over.

payload.description: Loop deficiency 17 (research loop): the two deep-recon runs of 2026-10-09 were chartered from the operator's questions alone, and the research firewall withheld project facts from the assistants, so the ADR and the greenfield brief folded in none of the standing plan: Epics 23 and 24 (open), the Phase 2 Hermes front door and its tk-submit/tk-status skills, the Phase 3 vertical-slice pack (playable-verify leg, asset ladder, run-vertical-slice job), the open DW entries and loop holes 3-16, and the recorded decision that Hermes profiles own live agent state (2026-09-01). The operator caught it at signature time and refused to sign. Hole to plug: the deep-recon charter and the ADR template gain a mandatory 'standing plan inventory' step (epics, DW ledgers, hole list, prior briefs, prior rulings) read before dimensions are cut and cited in the ADR's Context; the firewall keeps evidence clean but the synthesis step must reconcile against the inventory.

Loop deficiency 18 (plan status): tk-studio's canonical plan files (plan/ST-061.md to ST-072.md, index.md) still read status draft for Stories 20.1 to 22.5 although the loop landed them in the supervisor repository between 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-07 (599 tests, live on the box). The loop writes its own sprint state in the repository it builds in, and nothing pulls status back into the owning plan when the work lands elsewhere, so the plan index under-reports what is built (found by the 2026-10-09 design audit). Hole to plug: the supervisor's ended event with a PR URL triggers a plan-sync status pull-back on the owning project (a status-class field only, AD-5), or the close-out step of a loop run updates the canonical story in the plan that declared it.

payload.description: BMad core has moved to v6.12.0; studio pin sits at v6.11.0 — Run tk-studio-base-update to evaluate a bump to core 6.12.0. Before bumping, grep the studio plugin for direct references to 'bmad-checkpoint-preview' (not just the forwarding-shim id) since v6.12.0 renames it to bmad-walkthrough — any hard-coded skill/doc reference should move to the new id even though the shim covers runtime calls.

MCP spec 2026-07-28 is the largest revision in the protocol's history; governance moved to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation — If any tk-studio surface runs its own MCP server (planning backend, measurement, knowledge/research loop) or depends on a third-party one, check it against the 2026-07-28 spec's stateless-leaning changes before the next upstream server bump; also treat aaif.io (not anthropic.com) as the MCP governance source of record going forward.

Claude Code's October 2026 releases added marketplace plugin install, a plugin hook/mod system, and effort control for sub-agents — Before relying on specific version numbers or behavior claims above, pull github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md directly (gh api repos/anthropics/claude-code/contents/CHANGELOG.md) to confirm; if confirmed, evaluate the marketplace-install path as a distribution option for tk-studio itself, and the 'Claude Mods' hook system as a candidate mechanism for the studio's own status-surface work.

Loop-engineering community consensus: a loop needs maker/checker split, state outside context, stop conditions, budget limits, and an emergency kill switch before it's production-trustworthy — Map tk-studio's evolve/bmad-loop unattended runs against this checklist explicitly: jobrun.py's account/budget guard and AD-11's blocked-not-prompt rule cover stop-conditions and escalation, but confirm there is a distinct, explicit kill-switch primitive (not merely budget exhaustion) for operator-initiated abort of a running unattended loop.

'Session containment' is emerging as the named pattern for bounding an agent session's blast radius — Treat as informational only — no action needed unless a future finding shows tk-studio's per-run workspace / per-user store scoping diverges from this pattern. Worth a one-line note in the ecosystem-watch glossary rather than a driver change.

Loop deficiency 19 (launch planner): the Epic 25 launch bootstrap (run 20261014-195634-b06c) left two schema questions as Block If in plans/25-1.md and Open Questions in SPEC.md instead of settling them: the roster shape for components that have no release yet (supervisor, studio-web, cli) and the per-platform digest shape for uv and bun. The first dev session halted on them, the consult ruled escalate, and the run paused after one session (1.85M tokens, no work landed). The questions were answerable from the design spec and the ADR (never fabricate a digest; mise.lock-style per-platform pins) without a product decision. Hole to plug: the launch planner's SPEC step resolves schema shape for not-yet-existing artifacts (optional or deferred entries, per-platform maps) before the first story is dispatched, and the consult's scope text names schema shape as a planner matter rather than an operator ruling when the design documents already constrain it (the consult's own rule candidate says the same).

Loop deficiency 20 (launch, AD-11): the second launch of Epic 25 (relaunch after archiving a paused run with story 25-1 already done; cache epic-25-launch2, 11 turns, 38 s, USD 0.53) started the engine correctly (run 20261014-204241-9620 began 25-2) but its headless session ended with prose ('To watch it: run bmad-loop tui, check the ClaudeOS Queue, or run tk-studio-launch with verb status') and no terminal JSON status block, so a driver reading the result would record MISSING_STATUS_BLOCK for a run that succeeded. The first launch of the same epic ended with a correct block. The prose also names the retired ClaudeOS Queue. Hole to plug: the launch skill's relaunch path (stories already done, routing already applied) must end with the status block like the fresh path, and its watch hint should name the supervisor's status page instead of ClaudeOS; add a conformance drive for the relaunch case.
payload.evidence: .bmad-loop/cache/epic-25-launch2/launch.json (result text, no status block); .bmad-loop/cache/epic-25-launch1/launch.json (block present); runbook section 3.8 relaunch step

payload.description: Loop deficiency 21 (resolve, restore-patch): re-arming story 25-5 (run 20261014-221445-84de) with bmad-loop resolve --restore-patch failed on the first try: the rollback-auto step reverted tracked changes but left the dev session's new untracked files in place (they were not in the run's registered run-created list because the session halted mid-pass on a consult escalation), then git apply refused the patch with 'already exists in working directory' for every new file, and the run paused again (attempt-restore-failed). The attempt-worktree-preserved ref captured only tracked changes, so the preserved state was incomplete too. Recovery by hand: remove the leftover new files, rebuild the patch without the spec file, re-arm again. Hole to plug: rollback-auto should also remove untracked files that the attempt-preserve ref or the restore patch would recreate (or git apply should run with --3way or skip existing identical files), the preserve ref should include untracked new files, and the resolve path should name the collision and the fix in its pause reason.
